title: Attention dynamic-threshold regression during autoscale — mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During an autoscale-driven capacity surge on 2025-02-10 we observed a reproducible regression in p95 latency and tail throughput for certain attention-heavy workloads. The regression surfaced only under burst scaling (scale-up > 3x within 60s) and affected a small cohort of hosted customers using long-context chat models. Root interactions appear to be between the scheduler's transient probe behavior, the attention dynamic-threshold heuristic, and quantized kernel selection heuristics resulting in a higher-latency kernel being selected for many flows. This ticket consolidates investigation notes, mitigations already shipped, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.

metrics_observed:
- p95 latency: +2.7x on affected flows during burst (baseline 210ms -> 570ms)
- p50 unaffected or +10%
- throughput (requests/sec) dropped ~18% under mixed long-context load due to kernel misselection
- kernel switch rate increased by 240% during probe windows
- KV cache hit rate unchanged
root_cause_summary: The scheduler's probe window logic temporarily relaxes affinity to discover better paths when load patterns change. For attention-heavy, long-context requests this coincided with the attention dynamic-threshold heuristic deciding a different execution path (favoring a lower-memory but higher-latency quantized kernel) because the heuristics saw short-term signal that favored memory savings. The combined effect produced rapid kernel churn and increased serialization inside the execution pipeline, raising p95. Two contributing factors: (1) insufficient hysteresis between probe-induced path probing and attention threshold adjustments, and (2) kernel ranking did not account for transient latency variance under autoscale bursts.
mitigations_completed: Pinned kernel selection to stable ranking during probe windows (hotfix PR #4821)
Added temporary guard: disable attention threshold changes during scale-up window
Enhanced probe window telemetry to emit kernel selection decision traces to NewRelic dashboard

rollout_plan: 1) Merge kernel-ranking score change behind feature flag. 2) Run canary in isolated canary cluster with increased long-context synthetic load for 48h. 3) If stable, enable feature flag for 10% of hosted traffic for 24h and monitor kernel-switch-rate/p95. 4) Ramp to 50% then 100% with automated rollback if any of the hard SLO thresholds are breached. Rollbacks will revert to pinned selection behavior rolled out in hotfix.
verification_steps: Run synthetic burst harness with long-context chat mix and verify p95 <= 1.2x baseline
Confirm kernel-switch-rate stays within 10% of baseline during scale-up window
Smoke test KV cache and end-to-end latency on representative customer payloads
Coordinate with SRE to validate alerting and runbooks
